G2300.def:
θεάομαι, -ῶμαι 
[in LXX; 2 Chroniques 22:6 (רָאָה), Tob.2:2 13:6, 14, Jdth.15:8, 2Ma.2:4 2Mac 3:36, 3Ma.5:47 * ;] 
to behold, look upon, contemplate, view (in early writers with a sense of wondering), in NT apparently always in literal, physical sense of "careful and deliberate vision which interprets . . . its object": with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 11:7, Luc 7:24 23:55, Jean 1:14, 32 4:35 11:45, Actes 22:9, 1 Jean 1:1; with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 22:11, Actes 21:27, Romains 15:24, 1 Jean 4:12; with ptcp., Marc 16:14, Luc 5:27, Jean 1:38, Actes 1:11; before ὅτι, Jean 6:5, 1 Jean 4:14; pass., Matthieu 6:1 23:5, Marc 16:11.†
SYN.: see: θεωρέω

G2301.def:
θεατρίζω
(θέατρον), 
to make a spectacle of, expose to contempt (eccl.; ἐκθ-, Polyb.): pass., Hébreux 10:33.†

G2302.def:
θέατρον, -ον, τό
(θεάομαι), 
__1. a theatre (used also as a place of assembly): Actes 19:29, 31. 
__2. Collective for οἱ θεαταί, the spectators. 
__3. = θέα, θέαμα, a spectacle, show: metaphorically, 1 Corinthiens 4:9.†

G2303.def:
θεῖον, -ου, τό 
[in LXX; Genèse 19:24, Deutéronome 29:23 Job 18:15, Psaumes 11:7, Ésaïe 30:33 34:9, Eze.38:22 (גׇּפְרִית), 3Ma.2:5 * ;] 
brimstone: Luc 17:29 (LXX), Apocalypse 9:17-18 14:10 19:20 20:10 21:8.†

G2304.def:
θεῖος, -εία, -εῖον
(θεός), [in LXX: Exode 31:3 35:31, Job 27:3 33:4, Proverbes 2:17 (אֵל, אֱלֹהִים, אֱלוֹהַּ), Sir.6:35, 1-37 II Malachie 3:1-40, 3Ma.1:1-29, 4Mac.25 * ;] 
divine: δύναμις, 2 Pierre 1:3; φύσις (for parallel in π., see MM, Exp., xv), 2 Pierre 1:4; τὸ θ., 
the Deity (so in cl.; of God, in Philo and FlJ), Actes 17:29.†

G2305.def:
θειότης, -ητος, ἡ 
(θεῖος) [in LXX: Wis.18:9 * ;] 
divine nature, divinity: Romains 1:20 (for ex. from π., see MM, Exp., xv).†
SYN.: θεότης, deity, godhead, divine personality. θει. = divine nature and properties, a summary term for the attributes of deity, differing from θεότης as quality or attribute from essence

G2307.def:
θέλημα, -τος, τό
(θέλω), [in LXX chiefly for חָפֵץ, also for רָצוֹן, etc. ;] 
will, 
__(a) objectively = that which is willed: Matthieu 18:14, Luc 12:47, Jean 5:30, 1 Corinthiens 7:37, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:18, 2 Timothée 2:26, Hébreux 10:10, Apocalypse 4:11; θ. τ. θεοῦ, Actes 22:14, Romains 2:18 12:2, Éphésiens 1:9, Colossiens 1:9 4:12, 1 Pierre 4:2; τ. κυρίου, Éphésiens 5:17; pl., of precepts, Marc 3:35, WH, mg., Actes 13:22 (LXX); ἐστιν τὸ θ., with genitive of person(s), before ἵνα, Jean 6:39-40, 1 Corinthiens 16:12; with inf., 1 Pierre 2:15; with accusative and inf., 1 Thessaloniciens 4:3 
__(b) subjectively = τὸ θέλειν (cf. θέλησις): Luc 23:25, Jean 1:13, 1 Pierre 3:17, 2 Pierre 1:21; ποιεῖν, Matthieu 7:21 12:50 21:31, Marc 3:35 (pl., WH, mg., see supr.), Jean 4:34 6:38 7:17 9:31, Éphésiens 6:6, Hébreux 10:7, 9 10:36 13:21, 1 Jean 2:17; γίνεσθαι, Matthieu 6:10 26:42, Luc 22:42, Actes 21:14; ἡ εὐδοκία ( βουλὴ) τοῦ θ., Éphésiens 1:5, 11; ἐν τῷ θ. τοῦ θεοῦ, Romains 1:10; διὰ θ. θεοῦ, Romains 15:32, 1 Corinthiens 1:1, 2 Corinthiens 1:1 8:5, Éphésiens 1:1, Colossiens 1:1, 2 Timothée 1:1; κατὰ τὸ θ. τ. θεοῦ, Galates 1:4, 1 Pierre 4:19, 1 Jean 5:14; pl., Éphésiens 2:3 (Cremer, 728).†

G2308.def:
θέλησις, -εως, ἡ
(θέλω) [in LXX: 2 Chroniques 15:15, Proverbes 8:35 (רָצוֹן), Eze.18:23 (חֵפֶץ), LXX Daniel 11:45 (צְבִי), Tob.12:18, Wis.16:25, 2Ma.12:16, 3Ma.2:26 * ;] 
in colloq. and MGr. = τὸ θέλειν, 
will: Hébreux 2:4.†

G2309.def:
θέλω (the strengthened form ἐθέλω is found in Hom., and is the more frequently in Attic; see Rutherford, NPhr., 415f.), 
[in LXX for חפץ ,אבה; with neg., מאן pi., etc. ;] 
to will, be willing, wish, desire (more frequently than βούλομαι, which see, in vernac. and late Gk., also in MGr.; for various views as to its relation to β., see Thayer, 286; but see also BL, §24, see word): absol., Romains 9:16, 1 Corinthiens 4:19 12:18, Jacques 4:15; τ. θεοῦ θέλοντος, Actes 18:21; with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 20:21, Marc 14:36, Jean 15:7, Romains 7:15, 16 1 Corinthiens 4:21 7:36, Galates 5:17; with inf., Matthieu 5:40, Marc 10:43, Jean 6:21, 67 Romains 7:21, Galates 4:9; with accusative and inf., Marc 7:24, Luc 1:62, Jean 21:22, 23 Romains 16:19, 1 Corinthiens 14:5, Galates 6:13; οὐ θέλω, Matthieu 18:30, al.; id. with inf., Matthieu 2:18, Marc 6:26, Jean 5:40, 1 Corinthiens 16:7; before ἵνα, Matthieu 7:12, Marc 6:25, Jean 17:24; opposite to ποιέω, πράσσω, ἐνεργέω, Romains 7:15, 19 2 Corinthiens 8:10, 11 Philippiens 2:13; before ἤ (ICG, in l.; Deiss., LAE, 179:24), 1 Corinthiens 14:19; θέλων ἐν ταπεινοφροσυνῄ (of his own mere will, by humility, R, mg), Colossiens 2:18; in OT quotations, for Heb. חפץ, with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 27:43; with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 9:13 12:7, Hébreux 10:5, 8; with inf., 1 Pierre 3:10; for אמר, with inf., Actes 7:28 (see Cremer, 726ff.). 
θέλω (the strengthened form ἐθέλω is found in Hom., and is the more frequently in Attic; see Rutherford, NPhr., 415f.), 
[in LXX for חפץ ,אבה; with neg., מאן pi., etc. ;] 
to will, be willing, wish, desire (more frequently than βούλομαι, which see, in vernac. and late Gk., also in MGr.; for various views as to its relation to β., see Thayer, 286; but see also BL, §24, see word): absol., Romains 9:16, 1 Corinthiens 4:19 12:18, Jacques 4:15; τ. θεοῦ θέλοντος, Actes 18:21; with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 20:21, Marc 14:36, Jean 15:7, Romains 7:15, 16 1 Corinthiens 4:21 7:36, Galates 5:17; with inf., Matthieu 5:40, Marc 10:43, Jean 6:21, 67 Romains 7:21, Galates 4:9; with accusative and inf., Marc 7:24, Luc 1:62, Jean 21:22, 23 Romains 16:19, 1 Corinthiens 14:5, Galates 6:13; οὐ θέλω, Matthieu 18:30, al.; id. with inf., Matthieu 2:18, Marc 6:26, Jean 5:40, 1 Corinthiens 16:7; before ἵνα, Matthieu 7:12, Marc 6:25, Jean 17:24; opposite to ποιέω, πράσσω, ἐνεργέω, Romains 7:15, 19 2 Corinthiens 8:10, 11 Philippiens 2:13; before ἤ (ICG, in l.; Deiss., LAE, 179:24), 1 Corinthiens 14:19; θέλων ἐν ταπεινοφροσυνῄ (of his own mere will, by humility, R, mg), Colossiens 2:18; in OT quotations, for Heb. חפץ, with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 27:43; with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 9:13 12:7, Hébreux 10:5, 8; with inf., 1 Pierre 3:10; for אמר, with inf., Actes 7:28 (see Cremer, 726ff.).

G2310.def:
θεμέλιος, -ον
(τίθημι), [in LXX for אַרְמוֹן, מוֹסָד, etc. ;] 
of or for a foundation; as subst., ὁ θ. (sc. λίθος), a foundation stone, foundation: Luc 6:48-49 14:29 (but see Deiss., BS, 123); pl., οἰ θ. (cl.), Hébreux 11:10 Apocalypse 21:14, 19; neut., τὸ θ. (Arist., Phys., vi, 6, 10, LXX and later writers), Actes 16:26; metaphorically, Romains 15:20, 1 Corinthiens 3:10-12 Éphésiens 2:20, 1 Timothée 6:19, 2 Timothée 2:19, Hébreux 6:1.†

G2311.def:
θεμελιόω, -ῶ 
[in LXX chiefly for יָסַד ;] 
to lay the foundation of, to found: with accusative, τ. γῆν, Hébreux 1:10 (LXX); pass., Matthieu 7:25, Luc 6:48; metaphorically, 1 Pierre 5:10 (R, mg., settle); pass., Éphésiens 3:18, Colossiens 1:23.†

G2312.def:
θεο-δίδακτος, -ον 
taught of God (cf. διδακτοὶ θεοῦ, Jean 6:45): 1 Thessaloniciens 4:9.†

G2313.def:
θεομαχέω, -ῶ
(θεομάχος), [in LXX: 2Ma.7:19 * ;] 
to fight against God: Actes 23:9 (Rec.).†

G2314.def:
θεομάχος, -ον 
[in Sm.: Job 26:5, Proverbes 9:18 21:16 * ;] 
fighting against God: Actes 5:39.†

G2315.def:
θεόπνευστος, -ον
(θεός, πνέω), 
inspired by God: 2 Timothée 3:16.†

G2316.def:
θεός, -οῦ, ὁ, ἡ (Actes 19:37 only; see M, Pr., 60, 244), late voc., θεέ (Matthieu 27:46; cf. Deutéronome 3:24, al.), 
[in LXX chiefly for אֱלֹהִים, also for אֵל and other cognate forms, יהוה, etc. ;] 
a god or deity, God. 
__1. In polytheistic sense, a god or deity: Actes 28:6, 1 Corinthiens 8:4, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:4, al.; pl., Ac. 14:11 19:26, Galates 4:8, al. 
__2. Of the one true God; 
__(a) anarthrous: Matthieu 6:24, Luc 20:38, al.; esp. with prep. (Kühner 3, iii, 605), ἀπὸ θ., Jean 3:2; ἐκ, Actes 5:39, 2 Corinthiens 5:1, Philippiens 3:9; ὑπό, Romains 13:1; παρὰ θεοῦ, Jean 1:6; παρὰ θεῷ, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:6, 1 Pierre 2:4; κατὰ θεόν, Romains 8:27, 2 Corinthiens 7:9, 10; also when in genitive dependent on an anarth. noun (Bl., §46, 6), Matthieu 27:43, Luc 3:2, Romains 1:17, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:13; as pred., Lk 20:38, Jean 1:1, and when the nature and character rather than the person of God is meant, Actes 5:29, Galates 2:6, al. (M, Th., 14); 
__(b) more freq., with art.: Matthieu 1:23, Marc 2:7, al. mult.; with prep., ἀπὸ τ. θ., Luc 1:26; ἐκ, Jean 8:42, al.; παρὰ τοῦ θ., Jean 8:40; π. τῷ θ., Romains 9:14; ἐν, Colossiens 3:3; ἐπὶ τῷ θ., Luc 1:47; ἐπὶ τὸν θ., Actes 15:19; εἰς τ. θ., Actes 24:15; πρὸς τ. θ., Jean 1:2; with genitive of person(s), Matthieu 22:32, Marc 12:26, 27, Luc 20:37, Jean 20:17, al.; ὁ θ. μου, Romains 1:8, Php 1:3, al.; ὁ θ. καὶ πατήρ κ. τ. λ., Romains 15:6, Éphésiens 1:3, Phi 4:20, al.; with genitive of thing(s), Romains 15:5, 13, 33, 2 Corinthiens 1:3, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:23; τὰ τ. θεοῦ, Matthieu 16:23, Marc 12:17, 1 Corinthiens 2:11; τὰ πρὸς τὸν θ., Romains 15:17, Hébreux 2:17 5:1; τ. θεῷ, as a superl. (LXX, Josué 3:3), Actes 7:20, 2 Corinthiens 10:4; Hebraistically, of judges (Psa.81(82):6), Jean 10:34" (LXX), 35.

G2317.def:
θεοσέβεια, -ας, ἡ
(θεοσεβής), [in LXX Genèse 20:11 (אֱלֹהִים יִרְאָה), Job 28:28 (אֲדֹנָי id.), Sir.1:24, Bar.5:4, 4Ma.7:6 4Mac 7:22, א 4Ma.15:28 א 4Ma.17:15 * ;] 
fear of God, godliness: 1 Timothée 2:10.†

G2318.def:
θεοσεβής, -ές
(θεός, σέβομαι), [in LXX for אֱלֹהִים יָרֵא, Exode 18:21, al. ;] 
God-fearing, godly: Jean 9:31.†
SYN.: εὐσεβής (which see), θρῆσκος

G2319.def:
θεοστυγής, -ές
(θεός, στυγέω), 
__1. passive, as frequently in cl., hateful to God: Romains 1:30 (R, txt., cf. Lit., Notes, 256). 
__2. Active, hating God: lb. (R, mg., cf. ICC, in l).†

G2320.def:
θεότης, -ητος, ἡ 
deity, Godhead: Colossiens 2:9†
SYN.: θειότης, q.v

G2322.def:
θεραπεία, -ας, ἡ
(θεραπεύω) [in LXX for עֶבֶד Genèse 45:16 (cf. Esther 5:2), etc. ;] 
__1. service. 
__2. healing: Luc 9:11 (Field, Notes, 60), Apocalypse 22:2. 
__3. Collective, household attendants, servants: Luc 12:42 (LXX, ll. with).†

G2323.def:
θεραπεύω 
[in LXX for יָשַׁב, etc. ;] 
__1. to do service, serve: with accusative of person(s), pass., Actes 17:25. 
__2. As medical term, to treat (MM, Exp., xv), cure, heal: Matthieu 12:10, Marc 6:5, Luc 6:7, al.; with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 4:24, Marc 1:34, al.; before ἀπό, Luc 5:15 6:18 7:21 8:2, 43; θ. νόσον (μαλακίαν), Matthieu 4:23, al 
SYN: ἰάομαι (see Field, Notes, 60; MM, Exp., l.with)

G2324.def:
θεράπων, -οντος, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for עֶבֶד ;] 
an attendant, servant: Hébreux 3:5 (LXX)
SYN.: see: διάκονος

G2325.def:
θερίζω
(θέρος), [in LXX chiefly for קָצַר ;] 
to reap: Matthieu 6:26, Luc 12:24, Jacques 5:4; figuratively, Matthieu 25:24, 26, Luc 19:21-22, Jean 4:36-38, 2 Corinthiens 9:6, Galates 6:7, 9, Apocalypse 14:15; with accusative, τ. σαρκικά, 1 Corinthiens 9:11; φθοράν, ζωὴν αἰώνιον, Galates 6:8; τ. γῆν, Apocalypse 14:16.†

G2327.def:
θεριστής, -οῦ, ὁ
(θερίζω), [in LXX: Dan LXX Bel 1:32, Th Bel 1:33* ;] 
a reaper: Matthieu 13:30, 39†

G2328.def:
θερμαίνω
(θερμός), [in LXX chiefly for חָמַם ;] 
to warm, heat; mid., to warm oneself: Marc 14:54, 67, Jean 18:18, 25 Jacques 2:16.†

G2329.def:
θέρμη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX: Job 6:17, Psaumes 19:6, Ecclésiaste 4:11 (חָמַם and derivatives), Sir.38:28 * ;] 
heat: Actes 28:3.†

G2330.def:
θέρος, -ους, τό
(θέρω, to heat), [in LXX chiefly for קַיִץ ;] 
summer: Matthieu 24:32, Marc 13:28, Luc 21:30.†

G2331.def:
θεσσαλονικεύς, -έως, ὁ 
a Thessalonian: Actes 20:4 27:2, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:1, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:1.†

G2332.def:
θεσσαλονίκη, -ης, ἡ 
Thessalonica, a city of Macedonia: Actes 17:1, 11 17:13, Philippiens 4:16, 2 Timothée 4:10.†

G2333.def:
Θευδᾶς
(perh. contr. from Θεόδωρος, but see MM, Exp., xv), -ᾶ, ὁ 
Theudas: Actes 5:36.†

G2334.def:
θεωρέω, -ῶ
(θεωρός, a spectator, θεάομαι) [in LXX chiefly for רָאָה, חָזָה ;] (present and imperfect only, exc. Jean 7:3 (fut.), Matthieu 28:1, Luc 23:48, Jean 8:51, Apocalypse 11:12 (aor.); El., § 24); 
__1. (cl.), to look at, gaze, behold: absol., Matthieu 27:55, Marc 15:40, Luc 23:35; before πῶς, Marc 12:41; ποῦ, Marc 15:47; with accusative of person(s), Jean 6:40, 62 12:45 16:10-19, Actes 3:16 20:38 25:24, Apocalypse 11:11-12; id. with ptcp., Marc 5:15, Luc 10:18, Jean 6:19 10:12 20:12, 14, 1 Jean 3:17; with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 28:1, Luc 14:29 21:6 23:48, Jean 2:23 6:2 7:3, Actes 4:13 8:13; id. with ptcp., Jean 20:6, Actes 7:56 10:11; before ὅτι, Actes 19:26. 
__2. In popular lang. (Kennedy, Sources, 155; EL, § 24, see word ὁρᾶν), in present and imperfect = ὁράω, to see, perceive, discern: before ὅτι, Marc 16:4, Jean 4:19 12:19, Actes 19:26 27:10; πόσαι, Actes 21:20; πηλίκος, Hébreux 7:4; with accusative of thing(s), Marc 5:38; id. with ptcp., Actes 17:16 28:6; with accusative of person(s), Marc 3:11, Jean 14:19, Actes 9:7 17:22; πνεῦμα, Luc 24:37; τὸ π., Jean 14:17; before ὅτι, Jean 9:8; with ptcp., Luc 24:39. 
__3. Hebraistically, to experience, partake of: τ. θάνατον, Jean 8:51 (cf. Psaumes 89:49); τ. δόξαν, Jean 17:24 (cf. ἀνα-, παρα-θερρέω).†

G2335.def:
θεωρία, -ας, ἡ
(see: θεωρέω), [in LXX: Dan LXX 5:7, 2Ma.5:26 2Mac 15:12, 3Ma.5:24 * ;] 
__1. a viewing. 
__2. = θεώρημα, a spectacle, sight: Luc 23:48 (both senses in cl.).†

G2336.def:
Θήκη, -ης, ἡ
(τίθημι), [in LXX: Exode 25:27 (בַּיִת), Ésaïe 6:13 3:26 * ;] 
a receptacle, chest, case: of the sheath of a sword, Jean 18:11.†

G2337.def:
θηλάζω
(θηλή, a breast), [in LXX chiefly for יָנַק hi. ;] 
__1. of the mother, to suckle: Matthieu 24:19, Marc 13:17, Luc 21:23. 
__2. Of the young, to suck: Matthieu 21:16; μαστούς, Luc 11:27 (cf. Job 3:12, Cantique des cantiques 8:1, al.).†

G2338.def:
θῆλυς, -εια, -υ 
[in LXX chiefly for נְקֵבָה ;] 
female: as subst., ἡ θ., a female, a woman: Romains 1:26-27; τὸ θ.., Matthieu 19:4, Marc 10:6, Galates 3:28.†

G2339.def:
θήρα, -ας, ἡ 
[in LXX for צַיִד, טָרַף, רֶשֶׁת, and cogn. forms ;] 
__1. a hunting, chase (Hat., Xen., al.). 
__2. prey, game (c1.). 
__3. As in Psaumes 35:8 = רֶשֶׁת, a net: Romains 11:9 (but see Thayer, see word).†

G2340.def:
θηρεύω
(θήρα), [in LXX for צוּד, etc. ;] 
to hunt, ensnare, catch: metaphorically, Luc 11:54.†

G2341.def:
θηριομαχέω, -ῶ
(θηρίον, μάχομαι), 
to fight with wild beasts (Diod., al.): 1 Corinthiens 15:32.†

G2342.def:
θηρίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of θήρ), [in LXX chiefly for חַי ;] 
a wild beast, beast: Marc 1:13, Actes 11:6 28:4-5, Tite 1:12, Hébreux 12:20, Jacques 3:7, Apocalypse 6:8; of Antichrist, Apocalypse 11:7, 13-19.†

G2343.def:
θησαυρίζω 
[in LXX for צָפַן, etc. ;] 
to lay up, store up: of riches, Jacques 5:3; id. with dative of person(s), Luc 12:21, 2 Corinthiens 12:14; with accusative of thing(s), 1 Corinthiens 16:2; θησαυροὺς ἑαυτῷ, Matthieu 6:19-20; pass., 2 Pierre 3:7; metaphorically, ὀργὴν ἑαντῷ, Romains 2:5 (cf. Proverbes 1:18, Pss. Pss.Sol 9:9).†

G2345.def:
θιγγάνω 
[in LXX for נָגַע, Exode 19:12 * ;] 
__1. to touch, handle: Colossiens 2:21, Hébreux 12:20" (LXX) . 
__2. to injure (like Heb. נָגַע, and as in Eur., Iph. Aul., 1351): with genitive, Hébreux 11:28.†
SYN.: see: ἅπτω

G2346.def:
θλίβω 
[in LXX chiefly (ὁ θλίβων, ) for צוּר ;] 
to press: with accusative of person(s), Marc 3:9; ὁδὸς τεθλιμμένη, a narrow (compressed) way, Matthieu 7:14. Metaphorical (as frequently in LXX), to oppress, afflict, distress: with accusative of person(s), 2 Thessaloniciens 1:6; pass. (Vg., tribulor, tribulation em patior), 2 Corinthiens 1:6 4:8 7:5, 1 Thessaloniciens 3:4, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:7, 1 Timothée 5:10, Hébreux 11:37 (cf. ἀπο-, συν-θλίβω).†

G2347.def:
θλίψις (LTr., θλῖψις), -εως, ἡ 
(θλίβω), [in LXX for צָרָה, etc. ;] 
pressure (Arist.). In LXX and NT metaphorically, tribulation, affliction, distress: Matthieu 24:9, 21 24:29, Marc 13:19, 24, Jean 16:21, Actes 7:11 11:19, Romains 12:12, 2 Corinthiens 1:4 1:8 4:17 6:4 7:4 8:2 8:13, Philippiens 4:14, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:6, Jacques 1:27, Apocalypse 1:9 2:9, 22 7:14; with ἀνάγκη (which see), 1 Thessaloniciens 3:7; στενοχωρία (which from the order of the words would appear to be the stronger term), Romains 2:9 8:35; διωγμός, Matthieu 13:21, Marc 4:17, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:4; θ. ἔχω, Jean 16:33, 1 Corinthiens 7:23, Apocalypse 2:10; ἔρχεσθαι ἐπί, Actes 7:11; ἐν θλίψει 1 Thessaloniciens 1:6; pl., Actes 7:10 14:22 20:28, Romains 5:3, Éphésiens 3:13, 1 Thessaloniciens 3:3, Hébreux 10:33; τ. Χριστοῦ, Colossiens 1:24; θ. τῆς καρδίας, 2 Corinthiens 2:4; θ. ἐγείρειν, Philippiens 1:17.†
SYN.: ἀνάγκη, διωγμός, στενοχωρία (see supr., and cf. Tr., Syn, iv; Lft., Notes, 45)

G2348.def:
θνήσκω 
[in LXX chiefly for מוּת ;] 
to die; pf. (M, Pr., 114), to be dead: Matthieu 2:20, Marc 15:44, Luc 7:12 8:49, Jean 11:44 19:33, Actes 14:19 25:19; metaphorically, of spiritual death, 1 Timothée 5:6 (cf. ἀπο-, συν-απο-θνήσκω).†

G2349.def:
θνητός, -ή, -όν
(θνήσκω), [in LXX: Proverbes 3:13 20:24 (אָדָם), Job 30:23 (חַי), Ésaïe 51:12 (מוּת), Wis.9:14 15:17, 2Ma.9:12, 3Ma.3:29 * ;] 
subject to death, mortal: Romains 6:12 8:11, 1 Corinthiens 15:53-54, 2 Corinthiens 4:11 5:4.†

G2350.def:
θορυβέω, -ῶ
(θόρυβος), [in LXX: Nahum 2:3 (רָעַל ho.), Dan LXX 8:17 (בָּעַת ni.), Juges 3:26, Wis.18:19, Sir.40:6 * ;] 
__1. to make a noise or uproar: mid., of loud and ostentatious lamentation, Matthieu 9:23, Marc 5:39, Actes 20:10. 
__2. Trans., to trouble, throw into confusion: τ. πόλιν, Actes 17:5.†

G2351.def:
θόρυβος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX for הָמוֹן, etc. ;] 
a noise, uproar, tumult, as of an excited mob: Matthieu 26:5 27:24, Marc 14:2, Actes 20:1 21:34 24:18; of mourners, = ὄχλος θορυβούμενος, Marc 5:38.†

G2352.def:
θραύω 
[in LXX for 1,21 (Deutéronome 28:33, Ésaïe 42:4 58:6), etc. ;] 
to break in pieces, shatter; metaphorically, to break down: Luc 4:18 (LXX).†

G2353.def:
θρέμμα, -τος, τό
(τρέφω) 
__1. a nurseling, esp. of animals (Eur., Plat., al.). 
__2. cattle: Jean 4:12.†

G2354.def:
θρηνέω, -ῶ
(θρῆνος), [in LXX chiefly for יָלַל hi., also for קַיִן pit., etc. ;] 
__1. intrans., to lament, wail: Matthieu 11:17, Luc 7:32, Jean 16:20. 
__2. Trans., to bewail: with accusative of person(s), Luc 23:27.†
SYN.: κλαίω, κόπτομαι, λυπέομαι, πενθέω (see Tr., Syn., lxv).

G2355.def:
θρῆνος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for קִינָה ;] 
a lamentation: Matthieu 2:18, Rec.†

G2356.def:
θρησκεία (-κία, T), -ας, ἡ 
(θρῆσκος), [in LXX: Wis.14:18, 27, Sir.22:5 A, 4Ma.5:6 4Mac 5:13 * ;] 
religion in its external aspect (MM, Exp., xv), worship: Actes 26:5, Jacques 1:26-27; θ. τῶν ἀγγέλων, Colossiens 2:18.†
SYN.: see: θρῆσκος

G2357.def:
θρῆσκος
(-κός, WH), -ον, ό 
religious, careful of the outward forms of divine service (see previous word)): Jacques 1:26.†
SYN.: εὐσεβής, θεοσεβής, δεισιδαίμων (see Tr., Syn., § xlviii)

G2358.def:
θριαμβεύω
(θρίαμβος, 1. a festal hymn to Bacchus. 2. The Roman triumphus), 
__1. to triumph (and rarely, with accusative, to triumph over; so perh. Colossiens 2:15, but see infr.). 
__2. to lead in triumph: with accusative of person(s), 2 Corinthiens 2:14; hence, generally, to make a spectacle or show of: Colossiens 2:15 (but see supr.; cf. MM, Exp., xv; and esp. Field, Notes, 181).†

G2360.def:
θροέω, -ῶ
(θρόος, a noise, tumult), [in LXX: Cantique des cantiques 5:4 (הָמָה * ;] 
in cl., 
__1. to cry aloud, make an outcry. 
__2. to utter aloud. 
__3. In NT (and LXX), pass., to be troubled, as by an alarm: Matthieu 24:6, Marc 13:7, Luc 24:37 (WH, mg.), 2 Thessaloniciens 2:2 (cf. Kennedy, Sources, 126).†

G2361.def:
θρόμβος, -ου, ὁ
(τρέφω, in primary sense to thicken), 
a lump, a clot of blood (DCG, ii, 685b): αἵματος, Luc 22:44 (WH, R, mg. omit the passage, see WH, App., 64 ff.).†

G2362.def:
θρόνος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for כִּסֵּא, Exode 11:5, al. ;] 
in Hom., a seat, chair. Later, a throne, chair of state, seat of authority; of kings: metaphorically, of God, Matthieu 5:34, Actes 7:49" (LXX), Apocalypse 1:4, al.; by meton., for kingly power, sovereignty, Luc 1:32, 52, Actes 2:30; for an angelic hierarchy, Colossiens 1:16; of Christ, Matthieu 19:28, Apocalypse 3:21, al.; of Satan, Apocalypse 2:13; τ. θηρίου, Apocalypse 16:10; of the Apostles, Matthieu 19:28, Luc 22:30, cf. Apocalypse 20:4; of πρεσβύτεροι, Apocalypse 4:4 11:16 (on θ. τῆς χάριτος, Hébreux 4:16, see Westc., in l; Deiss., BS, 135)

G2363.def:
Θυάτειρα, -ων, τά
(-ας, ἡ, Apocalypse 1:11 L; cf. WH, App., 156) 
Thyatira, a city of Lydia: Actes 16:14, Apocalypse 1:11 2:18, 24.†

G2365.def:
θυγάτριον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of θυγάτηρ), 
a little daughter, a term of endearment used in late Gk. (cf. B1., § 27, 4): Marc 5:23 7:25.†

G2366.def:
θύελλα, -ης, ἡ
(θύω), [in LXX Deutéronome 4:11 5:22 (עֲרָפֶל), Exode 10:22 * ;] (poët. in cl.), 
a hurricane, cyclone, whirlwind: Hébreux 12:18.†
SYN.: λαίλαψ (which see)

G2367.def:
θύινος (usually θύϊνος, as Rec.), -η, -ον 
(θυία, θύα, an African aromatic tree, with ornamentally veined wood of varying colour, = Lat. citrinus), [in Sm.: 3Ki.10:11 (אַלְמֻגִּים)* ;] 
thyme: ξύλον, Apocalypse 18:12 (Diosc.).†

G2368.def:
θυμίαμα, -τος, τό
(θυμιάω), [in LXX chiefly for קְטֹרֶת ;] 
fragrant stuff for burning, incense: ἡ ὥρα τοῦ θ., Luc 1:10; θυσιαστήριον τοῦ θ. (Exode 30:27, al.), Luc 1:11; pl., Apocalypse 5:8 8:3-4 18:13.†

G2369.def:
θυμιατήριον, -ου, τό
(θυμιάω), [in LXX: 2 Chroniques 26:19, Eze.8:11 (קְטֹרֶת), 4Ma.7:11 * ;] 
__1. as in cl. (Hdt., iv, 162; Thuc., vi, 46) and LXX, a censer: Hébreux 9:4 (but see infr., and cf. Westc., in l). 
__2. As in Philo., rer. div., § 46, FlJ, Ant., iv, 2, 4, al., the altar of incense: He, l.with (but see supr. and cf. MM, Exp., xv).†

G2370.def:
θυμιάω, -ῶ
(θύω), [in LXX (with -άζω) chiefly for קָטַר pi., hi. ;] 
to burn incense: Luc 1:9.†

G2371.def:
θυμομαέω, -ῶ
(θυμός, μάχομαι), 
to fight desperately, have a hot quarrel: with dative of person(s), Actes 12:20.†

G2372.def:
θυμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(θύω), [in LXX most frequently for אַף, also for חֱמָא, חָרוֹן, etc., 30 words in all ;] 
passion, hot anger, wrath: Hébreux 11:27; ὀργὴ καὶ θ., Romains 2:8, cf. Colossiens 3:8; πικρία κ. θ., Éphésiens 4:31; πλησθῆναι, πλήρης θυμοῦ, Luc 4:28, Actes 19:28; θ. ἔχειν, Apocalypse 12:12; οἶνος τ. θυμοῦ τ. πορνείας (cf. Jérémie 51:7), Apocalypse 14:8 18:3 (cf. Apocalypse 17:2); οἶνος τ. θ. τ. θεοῦ, Apocalypse 14:10; τ. ὀργῆς τ. θεοῦ, Apocalypse 16:19 19:15; ὁ θ. τ. θεοῦ, Apocalypse 14:19 15:1, 7 16:1; pl., impulses or outbursts of anger: ἔρις, ζῆλος, θυμοὶ, ἐριθίαι, 2 Corinthiens 12:20, Galates 5:20 (Cremer, 287, 733).†
SYN.: ὀργή, παροργισμός

G2373.def:
θυμόω, -ῶ
(θυμός) [in LXX (chiefly in pass.) for חָרָה, אַף חָרָה hith., etc. ;] (no act. in Attic.); 
pass. (and mid.), 
to be wroth or very angry: Matthieu 2:16.†

G2374.def:
θύρα, -ας, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for פֶּתַח, also for דַּל, דֶּלֶת, etc. ;] 
a door: κλείειν (ἀποκ-) τὴν θ., Matthieu 6:6, Luc 13:25; pass., Matthieu 25:10, Luc 11:7, Jean 20:19, 26, Actes 21:30; ἀνοίγειν, Actes 5:19; pass., Actes 16:26-27; κρούειν, Actes 12:13; διὰ τῆς θ., Jean 10:1-2; πρὸς τὴν θ., Marc 1:33 11:4 (WH om. τήν), Actes 3:2; τὰ πρὸς τὴν θ., the space by the door, Marc 2:2; πρὸς τῇ θ., Jean 18:16; ἐπὶ τῇ θ, Actes 5:9; πρὸ τῆς θ., Actes 12:6; ἐπὶ τῶν θ., Actes 5:23; ἡ θ. τ. μνημείου, Matthieu 27:60, Marc 15:46 16:3. Metaphorical, of Christ, ἡ θ. τ. προβάτων, Jean 10:7, 9; of the Kingdom of Heaven, Luc 13:24; of opportunities, θ. πίστεως, Actes 14:27; θ. μεγάλη, 1 Corinthiens 16:9; θ. τ. λόγου, Colossiens 4:3; θ. ἀνεῳγμένη (ἠνεῳγ-), 2 Corinthiens 2:12, Apocalypse 3:8 4:1; of Christ, ἑστηκὼς ἐπὶ τὴν θ. καὶ κρούων, Apocalypse 3:20; of his second coming, ἐπὶ θύραις εἶναι, Matthieu 24:33, Marc 13:29; πρὸ θυρῶν ἑστηκέναι, Jacques 5:9.†

G2375.def:
θυρεός, -οῦ, ὁ
(θύρα), [in LXX for מָגֵן, צִנָּה ;] 
__1. in Hom., a door-stone. 
__2. In late Gk. (Polyb., Plut.), the scutum, a large oblong shield: θ. τ. πίστεως, Éphésiens 6:16 (cf. Wis.5:20, where ὁσιότης is likened to the ἀσπίς, the clypeus or small round shield of the light-armed soldier).†

G2376.def:
θυρίς, -ίδος, ἡ
(dim, of θύρα), [in LXX chiefly for חַלּוֹן ;] 
a window: Actes 20:9, 2 Corinthiens 11:33.†

G2377.def:
θυρωρός, -οῦ, ὁ, ἡ
(θύρα, + οὖρος, a guardian) [in LXX: 4Ki.7:11 (שׁוֹעֵר), Eze.44:11 (פְּקֻדָּה), 2 Rois 4:6 4:1 II Esther 7:1-28 * ;] 
a door-keeper, porter: ὁ, Marc 13:34, Jean 10:3; ἡ, Jean 18:16-17†

G2378.def:
θυσία, -ας, ἡ
(θύω) [in LXX chiefly for מִנְחָה, זָבַח ;] 
__1. actively, an offering, sacrifice (Hdt., al.) 
__2. Objectively, that which is offered, a sacrifice: Matthieu 9:13 12:7" (LXX), Marc 9:49 (WH, mg.), Éphésiens 5:2, Hébreux 10:5, 26; pl. (as usually in cl.), Marc 12:33, Luc 13:1, Hébreux 9:23 10:1, 8, (θ. καὶ προσφοράς); θ. ἀνάγειν, Actes 7:41; ἀναφέρειν, Hébreux 7:27; προσφέρειν, Actes 7:42, Hébreux 5:1 8:3 (δῶρά τε καὶ θ.) Hébreux 10:11-12 11:4; δοῦναι, Luc 2:24; pass., Hébreux 9:9; διὰ τῆς θ. αὐτοῦ, Hébreux 9:26; ἐσθίειν τὰς θ. (Lévitique 7:15 ff) 1 Corinthiens 10:18. Metaphorical, Philippiens 4:18, Hébreux 13:16; θ. πνευματικαί, 1 Pierre 2:5; θ. ζῶσα, Romains 12:1; θ. αἰνέσεως, Hébreux 13:15; θ. . . . τ. πίστεως, Philippiens 2:17.†

G2380.def:
θύω 
[in LXX chiefly for זָבַח, also for שָׁחַט, etc. ;] 
as in c1.; 
__1. to offer first fruits to a god. 
__2. to sacrifice by slaying a victim, offer sacrifice: Actes 14:13; with dative of person(s), Actes 14:18; id. with accusative of thing(s), 1 Corinthiens 10:20. 
__3. to slay, kill: Jean 10:10, Actes 10:13 11:7; with accusative of thing(s), Luc 15:23, 27 15:30; pass., Matthieu 22:4; τὸ πάσχα (Exode 12:21), Marc 14:12; pass., Luc 22:7, 1 Corinthiens 5:7.†

G2381.def:
θωμᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (Heb.: תָּאוֹם, a twin; cf. δίδυμος), 
Thomas the Apostle: Matthieu 10:3, Marc 3:18, Luc 6:15, Jean 11:16 14:5 20:24-28 21:2, Actes 1:13.†

G2382.def:
θώραξ, -ακσς, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for שִׁרְיוֹן and cogn. forms ;] 
a breastplate: Apocalypse 9:9, 17; θ. τ. δικαιοσύνης, Éphésiens 6:14 (cf. Ésaïe 59:17, Wis.5:18-19); θ. πίστεως, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:8.†

G2383.def:
Ἰάειρος, -ου, ὁ (Heb. יָאִיר, Nombres 32:41), 
Jairus: Marc 5:22, Luc 8:41.†

G2384G.def:
Ἰακώβ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. יַעֲקֹב), 
Jacob; 
__1. The patriarch: Matthieu 1:2 8:11, Jean 4:5-6, Actes 7:8, al; as in Heb. (cf. Nombres 23:7, Ésaïe 41:8, Sir.23:12, al.), of his descendants, Romains 11:26 (LXX). 
__2. The father-in-law of Mary: Matthieu 1:15-16 (on the form as distinct from that of the next word, see Deiss., BS, 3161)

G2384H.def:
Ἰακώβ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. יַעֲקֹב), 
Jacob; 
__1. The patriarch: Matthieu 1:2 8:11, Jean 4:5-6, Actes 7:8, al; as in Heb. (cf. Nombres 23:7, Ésaïe 41:8, Sir.23:12, al.), of his descendants, Romains 11:26 (LXX). 
__2. The father-in-law of Mary: Matthieu 1:15-16 (on the form as distinct from that of the next word, see Deiss., BS, 3161)

G2385G.def:
Ἰάκωβος, -ου, ὁ (Heb., see previous word) 
James; 
__1. Son of Zebedee: Matthieu 4:21, Marc 1:19, 29, Actes 1:13 12:2, al. 
__2. Son of Alphæus: Matthieu 10:3, Marc 2:14, al.; commonly identified with Ἰ. ὁ μικρός, James the little, son of Mary (see: Μαρία, 3; Κλωπᾶς), Matthieu 27:56, Marc 15:40 16:1 (cf. Jean 19:25). 
__3. The Lord's brother (see: ἀδελφός): Matthieu 13:55, Marc 6:3, Actes 12:17, al., 1 Corinthiens 15:7 (probably), Galates 1:19 2:9, 12, Jacques 1:1, Ju 1. 
__4. The father of the apostle, Ἰούδας Ἰακώβου: Luc 6:16, Actes 1:13

G2385H.def:
Ἰάκωβος, -ου, ὁ (Heb., see previous word) 
James; 
__1. Son of Zebedee: Matthieu 4:21, Marc 1:19, 29, Actes 1:13 12:2, al. 
__2. Son of Alphæus: Matthieu 10:3, Marc 2:14, al.; commonly identified with Ἰ. ὁ μικρός, James the little, son of Mary (see: Μαρία, 3; Κλωπᾶς), Matthieu 27:56, Marc 15:40 16:1 (cf. Jean 19:25). 
__3. The Lord's brother (see: ἀδελφός): Matthieu 13:55, Marc 6:3, Actes 12:17, al., 1 Corinthiens 15:7 (probably), Galates 1:19 2:9, 12, Jacques 1:1, Ju 1. 
__4. The father of the apostle, Ἰούδας Ἰακώβου: Luc 6:16, Actes 1:13

G2385I.def:
Ἰάκωβος, -ου, ὁ (Heb., see previous word) 
James; 
__1. Son of Zebedee: Matthieu 4:21, Marc 1:19, 29, Actes 1:13 12:2, al. 
__2. Son of Alphæus: Matthieu 10:3, Marc 2:14, al.; commonly identified with Ἰ. ὁ μικρός, James the little, son of Mary (see: Μαρία, 3; Κλωπᾶς), Matthieu 27:56, Marc 15:40 16:1 (cf. Jean 19:25). 
__3. The Lord's brother (see: ἀδελφός): Matthieu 13:55, Marc 6:3, Actes 12:17, al., 1 Corinthiens 15:7 (probably), Galates 1:19 2:9, 12, Jacques 1:1, Ju 1. 
__4. The father of the apostle, Ἰούδας Ἰακώβου: Luc 6:16, Actes 1:13

G2385J.def:
Ἰάκωβος, -ου, ὁ (Heb., see previous word) 
James; 
__1. Son of Zebedee: Matthieu 4:21, Marc 1:19, 29, Actes 1:13 12:2, al. 
__2. Son of Alphæus: Matthieu 10:3, Marc 2:14, al.; commonly identified with Ἰ. ὁ μικρός, James the little, son of Mary (see: Μαρία, 3; Κλωπᾶς), Matthieu 27:56, Marc 15:40 16:1 (cf. Jean 19:25). 
__3. The Lord's brother (see: ἀδελφός): Matthieu 13:55, Marc 6:3, Actes 12:17, al., 1 Corinthiens 15:7 (probably), Galates 1:19 2:9, 12, Jacques 1:1, Ju 1. 
__4. The father of the apostle, Ἰούδας Ἰακώβου: Luc 6:16, Actes 1:13

G2386.def:
ἴαμα, -τος, τό
(ἰάομαι), [in LXX for מַרְפֵּא (2 Chroniques 36:16, Ecclésiaste 10:4, Jérémie 33:6, etc. ;] 
__1. most frequently in cl., a means of healing, remedy (Thuc., al.; Wis.11:4 10:9). 
__2. = ἴασις (which see), a healing (Plat.; Jer, l.with): pl., 1 Corinthiens 12:9 12:28 12:30.†

G2390.def:
ἰάομαι, -ῶμαι 
[in LXX for רָפָא (Genèse 20:17, al.), exc. Ésaïe 30:26 61:1 (חָבַשׁ) ;] 
to heal: with accusative of person(s), Luc 5:17 6:19 9:2, 11 9:42 14:4 22:51, Jean 4:47, Actes 9:34 10:38 28:8; pass., Matthieu 8:8, 13 15:28, Luc 7:7 8:47 17:15, Jean 5:13; id. before ἀπό᾽, Marc 5:29, Luc 6:17; figuratively, of spiritual healing, Matthieu 13:15, Jean 12:40, Actes 28:27" (LXX) ; pass., Hébreux 12:13, Jacques 5:16, 1 Pierre 2:24.†
SYN.: θεραπεύω, q.v

G2391.def:
Ἰάρετ (Rec. -ρέδ, L, Ἰάρεθ), ὁ (Heb. יֶרֶד, LXX Ἰάρεδ, FlJ, Ἰάρεδος), 
Jared (Genèse 5:15): Luc 3:37.†

G2392.def:
ἴασις, -εως, ἡ
(ἰάομαι), [in LXX chiefly for מַרְפֵּא ;] 
a healing, cure: Actes 4:22, 30; pl., Luc 13:32.†
SYN.: see: θεραπεία, 2; ἴαμα, 2

G2393.def:
ἴασπις, -ιδος, ἡ 
[in LXX: Exode 28:18 36:38 (Exode 39:11) (יַהֲלֹם), Ésaïe 54:12 (כַּדְכֹּד), Eze.28:13 (יָשְׁפֵה, see BDB, Lex., see word)* ;] 
jasper, apparently not the modern stone of that name, but a translucent stone (DB, see word): Apocalypse 4:3 21:11, 18-19.†

G2394.def:
Ἰάσων, -ονος, ὁ 
Jason: Actes 17:5-7, 9; perhaps the same, Romains 16:21.†

G2395.def:
ἰατρός, -οὔ, ὁ
(ἰάομαι), [in LXX for רָפָא ;] 
a physician: Matthieu 9:12, Marc 2:17 5:26, Luc 4:23 5:31 8:43 (om. WH, R, mg.), Colossiens 4:14 (on the status of physicians, see MM, Exp., xv.).†

G2396.def:
ἴδε (Attic ἰδέ; the "later" accentuation is also found in Hom.; Veitch, 215) 
__1. prop., 2 aor. imperat. of ὁράω, which see 
__2. As interjection, apart from the construction of the sentence, and used where one or many are addressed, see! behold! lo!: Matthieu 25:20, 22 25:25, Marc 2:24 3:34 11:21 13:1, 21 15:4, 35 16:6, Jean 1:29, 36 1:48 3:26 5:14 7:26 11:3, 36 12:19 16:29 18:21 19:4, 14 19:26-27, Galates 5:2.†

G2397.def:
ἰδέα, -ας, ἡ, see: εἰδέα 
εἰδέα (Rec. ἰδ-, as in cl.; see Tdf., Pr., 81), -ας, ἡ (εἶδον), [in LXX (seel. ἰδ-): Genèse 5:3 (דְּמוּת), Da TH 1:13, 15 (מַרְאֶה), Ep. Jer.63, 2Ma.3:16 * ;] 
appearance, look: Matthieu 28:3.†

G2399.def:
ἰδιώτης, -ου, ὁ
(ἴδιος), [in LXX: Proverbes 6:8 (no Heb.)* ;] 
__1. a pri­vate person, as opposite to the State or an official (βασιλεῖς κ. ἰδιῶται, Pr, l.with; and cf. MM, Exp., xv). 
__2. one without professional knowledge, unskilled, uneducated, unlearned: 1 Corinthiens 14:16 14:23-24 (R, mg., without gifts); ἀγράμματοι κ. ἰ., Actes 4:13; with dative (= cl. with genitive of thing(s)), λόγῳ, 2 Corinthiens 11:6.†
